USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Do not add another unscheduled escalation on top of the August 23 tariff-rate hike and the List 4 calendar already in motion. Keep existing Section 301 duties and the Huawei Entity List as leverage, but use the early-September Washington window to restart talks aimed at farm purchases plus a credible enforcement text. Further tariff ratcheting now would hit US consumers and the farm belt harder than it would force Beijing to concede structural issues.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is elevated but not existential. Since the failed Shanghai round (2019-07-30) the dispute has jumped from a paused Osaka truce to List 4 on the remaining ~$300B (2019-08-01), a currency-manipulator designation after CNY broke 7 (2019-08-05), and a same-day retaliation spiral on 2019-08-23 (China 5–10% on ~$75B including autos and farm goods; US order to raise List 4 to 15% and threaten hikes on existing lists). That cascade is already pricing into US conditions: 10-year yields fell to 1.47% on 2019-08-28 (from 2.72% in early March) and sit below the 2-year (1.50%), the first 2s10s inversion since 2007; VIX spiked to 24.59 on 2019-08-05 and was still 19.35 on 2019-08-28; Michigan sentiment collapsed from 98.4 in July to 89.8 in August. Ag is the exposed export sector: China told firms to stop buying US farm goods after August 1, 2018 soybean sales to China were already down ~74%, and Grassley plus the Farm Bureau warned of permanent market loss even as USDA aid runs toward $28B. Industrial production and CPI remain orderly, so this is high pressure—not a supply-chain or recession fait accompli—hence +0.38 rather than +0.5/+1.0. Action should stay near zero because the US already used its main tariff and non-tariff cards (List 3 at 25%, Huawei Entity List, manipulator label, List 4 split with 4B delayed to Dec 15 precisely to spare holiday consumer prices). Another escalate-tariffs move would likely draw more farm/auto retaliation and deepen the inversion/sentiment shock without a matching Chinese structural offer; unilateral rollback would throw away leverage after Beijing walked back the spring text and under-delivered Osaka farm purchases. Negotiate: hold the scheduled Sept 1 List 4A line, leave 4B and the Oct 1 30% threat as contingent bargaining chips, and test whether the G7-reported Chinese outreach to “get back to the table” can be converted into purchases plus enforcement language.
key_factors: August 2019 re-escalation after a failed Shanghai round and broken Osaka truce
US farm-belt exposure: China purchase halt, soybean market loss, Grassley/Farm Bureau political pressure
Market recession signal: 2s10s inversion, 10-year at 1.47%, VIX and consumer-sentiment collapse
List 4 already split (4A Sept 1 / 4B Dec 15) showing domestic consumer-cost constraint
Talks still formally open for early September; no Chinese structural concession yet that would justify rollback

sources_cited.excerpt: After the Shanghai round, Trump announces 10% tariffs on the remaining ~$300B of Chinese goods (List 4), effective Sept 1.
After CNY breaks 7 per USD, US Treasury designates China a currency manipulator (first such designation since 1994).
USTR splits List 4: List 4A effective Sept 1; List 4B (cell phones, laptops, toys, apparel) delayed to Dec 15.

China announces retaliation on ~$75B of US goods including re-imposing tariffs on US autos. Trump orders firms to look for an alternative to China and directs a 5-point increase on the planned List 4 rate.
Trade talks in Shanghai (through July 31). Little progress reported.
US 10-year yield 1.47% on 2019-08-28, down ~126 bp over the window; sits below the 2-year (1.50%).
Michigan consumer sentiment fell from 98.4 (July) to 89.8 (August).
VIX spiked to 24.59 on 2019-08-05 and closed 19.35 on 2019-08-28.
CNY/USD 7.1628 on 2019-08-28 after breaking 7 on August 5.

China raised tariffs on $75B of US goods including soybeans, pork and corn; Grassley warned farmers risk permanently losing an export market; China said Aug 5 that firms had stopped buying US farm products.
First 10-year/2-year inversion since 2007 on Aug 14; economists said a clear cessation of trade hostilities would be needed to reverse risk sentiment.
Shanghai talks ended with no deal; White House said negotiations were expected to continue in Washington in early September.

CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold the posture already announced on 23 August — the 5–10% duties on ~$75B of U.S. goods (including soy, pork, crude, and the Dec-15 auto restart) — and do not add a new tariff tranche, rare-earth cutoff, or live unreliable-entity designations this week. Keep the September deputy/principal channel open, but make no purchase or structural commitments until Washington freezes List 4 and walks back the 23 August hike-and-decouple order. Further escalation now would invite the threatened extra 5 points on List 4 and a broader U.S. corporate-exit campaign; unilateral rollback would ratify the U.S. breach of the Osaka “no new tariffs” understanding.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is high, not existential. Combined Section 301 coverage is about to reach essentially all Chinese goods sold to the U.S.: List 3 is already at 25% (10 May), List 4A lands 1 September, and List 4B plus a threatened lift of List 4 from 10% to 15% sit on the calendar after Trump’s 23 August order that U.S. firms “immediately start looking for an alternative to China.” Huawei remains on the Entity List (16 May); Google/GMS and U.S. chip suppliers cut off a national champion, and the 20 May Temporary General License expired 19 August with no removal from the list. CNY broke 7 on 5 August and traded 7.16 on 28 August — an 11-year low — after which Treasury labeled China a manipulator, adding a currency-war layer and outflow risk. Industrial production slowed to 4.4% y/y in August (4.8% in July), the weakest print in years, while CPI is firming. That maps to the CHN +0.5 anchor (export-sector hit, FX pressure, Huawei targeting) but not +1.0: reserves are still ~$3.13T and slightly up, merchandise exports remain ~$207B/month, and the yuan move itself cushions tariff incidence. Action stays at 0 because China has already used its remaining tariff ammunition (23 August $75B package, timed to U.S. List 4 dates) and because a second-round escalate would likely be answered by the threatened List-4 rate hike and a more literal decoupling push, while concede_purchases or any rollback would be unrequited — Shanghai (30–31 July) produced little progress and the U.S. has offered no matching freeze. Hold the announced measures, do not fire unused non-tariff tools yet, and let any September talks test whether Washington will de-escalate first.
key_factors: List 4A (1 Sep) plus threatened 15% rate and existing-list hikes after 23 Aug Trump order
Huawei Entity List still in force; TGL expired 19 Aug; Google/chip cutoff hits tech champion
CNY 7.16 / manipulator designation — buffer for exporters but capital-outflow and legitimacy risk
IP slowed to 4.4% y/y; reserves stable ~$3.13T so stress is real but not a financial crisis
China already announced $75B retaliation (soy, pork, crude, autos) — little tariff room left
Osaka no-new-tariffs understanding broken by U.S.; no matching U.S. offer that would justify purchases or rollback

sources_cited.excerpt: China announces retaliation on ~$75B of US goods (5–10%, split Sept 1 / Dec 15), including re-imposing tariffs on US autos. Trump orders US companies to immediately start looking for an alternative to China and directs a 5-point increase on the planned List 4 rate (to 15%) and threatened hikes on existing lists.
After the Shanghai round, Trump announces 10% tariffs on the remaining ~$300B of Chinese goods (List 4), effective Sept 1.
USTR splits List 4: List 4A effective Sept 1; List 4B delayed to Dec 15. Some sensitive items excluded.
After CNY breaks 7 per USD, US Treasury designates China a currency manipulator (first such designation since 1994).
US Commerce Department adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List. US firms generally barred from selling to Huawei without a license.
G20 Osaka: Trump and Xi agree to resume talks. Existing tariffs remain; no new tariffs for the time being. Trump says he will ease some Huawei restrictions (Huawei remains on the Entity List).
Trade talks in Shanghai (through July 31). Little progress reported.
China industrial production index 104.4 in Aug 2019 (4.4% y/y), down from 105.4 in April and 104.8 in July.
CNY/USD 7.1628 on 2019-08-28, up from ~6.70 in early March; broke 7 on 5 August.
China reserves ex-gold ~$3.126T in August, slightly higher over the window — no reserve-drain crisis yet.
China will impose additional 5% or 10% on 5,078 U.S. products including soybeans, crude oil; reinstituting 25% auto tariffs from Dec 15. Commerce Ministry: decision forced by U.S. unilateralism.
Google suspended Huawei Android/GMS; Qualcomm and Intel paused sales — a kill-switch risk for Huawei's international smartphone business.
Treasury: China took concrete steps to devalue while holding substantial reserves; Mnuchin will engage IMF; labeled a violation of G20 no-competitive-devaluation commitment.
China industrial production grew just 4.8% in July, the worst for that sector in 17 years.
